newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Oil Search still looking at Discovery.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Oil Search still looking at Discovery.

text.p: Oil Search Ltd said on Friday it would soon decide if it would bid for Discovery Petroleum NL after reviewing data from a due diligence examination.

"I have said for the last four weeks since we made the investment that a potential takeover of Discovery by Oil Search was one of a number of options that we would look at to maximise our investment," Oil Search managing director Peter Botten told Reuters on Friday from his Port Moresby office.
"That position has not changed, except that we have done a lot more work to look at the values," Botten said.

Sources involved in the Discovery takeover process told Reuters that Oil Search was likely to announce a takeover bid about mid-next week. "I would imagine something next week will come out (from Oil Search). It is an ongoing thing but I don't think it will sit on the shelf for much longer."

In late September, Oil Search paid 75 cents per share for a 10.1 percent stake in Discovery and at the time said a full bid was possible -- challenging a 70 cents per share hostile offer by Premier Oil Plc.
Premier has raised its bid to 80 cents, or A$104.2 million, but again faces rejection from the Perth-based Discovery.

Premier also conducted due diligence on Discovery's portfolio of Indonesian and Australian oil and gas acreage before making its latest offer. It said the 80 cent per share bid represented full value, but did not rule out another hike.
Share market speculators have constantly overbid the Premier offer price. Discovery shares ended one cent higher at 82 cents on Friday.
Brokers said recent investors expected a bid from Oil Search to be pitched at around 86 cents per share to be successful -- a price which Discovery has said would receive serious consideration.
